newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian security prices rise, call money inactive.
newsitem.headline: Indian security prices rise, call money inactive.

text.p: Prices of Indian government securities rose in brisk trade on Friday while overnight money was not traded, dealers said.
They said there were no trades in overnight money as it was the reporting day for banks. Dealers said three-day money was quoted 4.0-5.0 percent.
Prices of government securities rose in active trade, dealers said. Volumes traded on the National Stock Exchange went up to 2.4 billion rupees from 1.86 billion, they said.
"Prices went up as the market took a cue from the Reserve Bank of India's price-list," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
"As no more security issues are likely before the end of the current financial year, the market has taken the RBI's price-list as a benchmark for year-end valuation."

The 11.75 percent government of India stock traded on Friday at 94.75 rupees against its last traded 94.70, the 12 percent 1999 stock rose to 99.96 from 99.85, the 13.40 percent 1999 to 101.85 from 101.75 and the 13.70 percent 1999 to 102.81 from 102.75, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in March yielded 6.25 percent against its last traded 6.85 percent and April bill 7.50 percent against 7.60 percent, dealers said.
